blocks.content: The Constitution has made elaborate provisions to safeguard and ensure the independent and impartial functioning of the UPSC.

items: Removal on grounds of misbehaviour requires a mandatory inquiry by the Supreme Court, whose advice is binding on the President.
A member of UPSC is eligible to become Chairman of UPSC or SPSC, but is ineligible for any other government post.
UPSC expenses are non-votable by Parliament because they are charged directly on the Consolidated Fund of India.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Security of tenure is guaranteed to the Chairman and members of UPSC, who can be removed only under constitutional provisions.
Salaries, allowances, and pensions are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India and are not subject to a vote in Parliament.
The Chairman of UPSC is strictly ineligible for any further employment under the Government of India or any State Government.
Conditions of service of members cannot be varied to their disadvantage after their appointment.
